A slot can read more than one holon: what an expression gathers. An expression is a function given what it takes, data held in a body like any other, and the engine evaluates it to the holons it gathers, in the field's order. It is a holon, `{ $ref: H }`, a set of one; a call, `{ call: P, with: [ … ] }`, the function P given its arguments; or, within a function of one's own, `{ arg: i }`, what it was given. Every function is a holon of the type Function. Glass's own are native, run by the engine: Everything; Type, the instances of the types given; Children of and Parents of, what the holons given point to and what points to them; Text, what contains each word given; Store; Has a name; Is a type; And, Or and Not; and Group by. Each takes sets, which are expressions, so they compose as deep as one likes, Not: Children of: Type: Brief as it reads, or words, as a store's key or an axis. A function of one's own gives an expression over what it is given, so it is called as glass's are and stands beside them. Held in a mount, an expression is what the mount gives, and a component may gather in what it reads, so the same field can be looked at from as many angles as there are expressions, each drawn by whatever takes it.

Gathered, a set is flat, and a flat field is never what one wants to see. So Group by gives what it is given in collections besides, one for each value along an axis: type, parent or store. Each collection is itself an expression, the first narrowed by one value and grouped again automatically, so it opens like any place, in layers; layer by layer, the field is entered as it is made. Grouped automatically, the field chooses: for whatever is gathered it takes the axis that gives a few groups, three to a dozen, covering most of it, and where nothing splits a set, or every holon shares a value, it is given as it is. The root gives the field's roots: what nothing references, `Not(Children of(Everything))`, a pure expression and no function of its own. A holon that holds others is their group, so the field shows only the tops of its trees, a few dozen holons, each opened to go down; all of glass's briefs stand under one of them, Glass. Grouped by type, a holon nothing holds still collects under what it is, as orphans would. References build direction, from what holds to what is held; instanceship, from an instance to its type, groups crosswise and makes nothing anyone's child, so types do not swallow their instances. As built, every reference counts as holding, a mention in prose among them; once a reference says whether it holds, as [the relations](ref:01M6M9PESEMJ7TCJR619DND3DV) decide, Children of reads holding alone and the roots are what nothing holds.

// opened: Function (8), Component (6), Type (4), Mount (2), Brief (1: Glass), …

None of the families is a medium for programs and interfaces as well as data, and none has types that govern what may be written. That is what OpenLight adds, and it lives in the object model, so the object model is glass's own: holons with ids, versions, an index, commits and refs.

A version holds what the store needs and the holon's body: the holon's id, the version before it, what the holon is an instance of, and its body. The body is whatever the holon holds, shaped by its types: a brief's title and prose live there, as a track's title and length would. Versions are the atoms: everything else in the store only points at them.

```json
{ "kind": "version", "id": "01JB…store", "prev": "sha256-27…",
  "instance": ["01JA…brief"],
  "body": { "title": "The store", "prose": "A store is where a field is kept …" } }
```

Every object says what kind it is, so any one of them can be read alone, by a person browsing the files or a program checking them, without knowing how it was reached.

*The author's, 2026-11-02: a holon is what the storage needs and then its body, and title and prose go into the body. Keeping `kind` the session's.*

A version is to hold two more of what the storage needs, out of the body: the holon's name, and, if it is a type, its mould, the fields its instances hold, each with its prose and the shape the engine checks. The body then holds only what the holon holds itself, and a holon is a type by having a mould, an instance of nothing to be one; the type of types is let go. Not yet built: [the vectors](ref:01M6F8G0M08YW99CZCT2A6Q4CF), the store and the engine change with it, and `either`, a union, is a shape the engine does not yet know.

  "instance": [],
  "mould": { "text": { "says": "What it says: words, and the references among them, to where they lead, a Term or an Emphasis.",

Glass keeps the field in a store anyone can serve as plain files, and puts the engine and the interface in a client that pulls the store and runs over it, in the reader's own browser.

Any relation a holon has to another is a reference in its body, under a key its type gives meaning to: a note's `about`, a role's `who` and `where`, a run's `program`. A reference is written the same way wherever it stands, so it is seen as one without knowing the type, by a reader or by the engine, even when the type is in a store neither has. Types say what a reference means and check it; they are never what finds it.

A reference points at a holon's identity, so it follows the holon as it changes, or it is pinned to one version, so it keeps saying what it said: a note pins the version of the brief it was written against.

Glass's store is the native one, its format the one the engine speaks without translating, so its holons need none; files on a disk, files over HTTP and a peer streaming live are only ways of reaching it. A git repository, the browser's history or a video's high-fidelity data are integrations with formats better suited to them, never copied into glass's store, each wherever the engine runs supplying it.

What an integration allows is its own to say: to be only read, or written through its programs, and how. A holon pointing into one may be pinned, as a reference to a file is pinned to the git commit it was read at.

*The author's, 2026-11-04: why can't the stores we are talking about be the same first-class citizen as the other integrations; it's up to the integration if you can manipulate the holons or not; a git repository is its own store, its own source of truth, you never include it into your own; is an integration just a program, his question carried from OpenLight. Format, transport and integration kept apart the session's. How git in particular is integrated, its files edited from the field, their content shown or only addressed, its commits meeting the field's, is open; so is what an integration's programs owe the engine, waiting for programs to run.*

To look somewhere else is a new address, a step in the browser's own history; back and forward are only the address changing, and nothing is written to go back, for commits are a line and are never undone. What the reader has looked at is kept in the field as their history, a holon in the home that each move adds a visit to, when and what, said as text, so a visit points at nothing that can be gone; going back adds none. This is where the browser and the field meet, an integration, kept in the interface until glass runs programs. A reader that is not the root, as one laid over another place, is a mount like any other, and needs no address. A mount found within what another draws, as the entry pressed in a list, is shown, not run: what it is called, the component it calls, and what it gives, pressed to look there; and a mount never moves to itself.

A press does not need catching from above. Every slot says where it is: its element carries the holons it reads as its location, and a link in prose carries the one it mentions. An index maps every holon's id to the version it has at that commit, and every name given in the store to the holon it names. It holds no content itself, only which state of each holon is current, so one index is the whole field at one moment.

```json
{ "kind": "index", "names": { "entry": "01JB…mount" }, "holons": "sha256-4c…" }
```

The holons are a tree split by the characters of their ids, read from the end, where ids are random. A leaf holds at most 64 holons; past that it becomes a branch over the next character, with a leaf or a branch beneath each. A change writes new nodes only on the way to the holons it touched, and shares every other node with the commit before, so the index stays light however large the field grows. The tree's shape depends only on which ids there are, so the same field always gives the same index, and two copies are compared by one name.

A commit is one change to the field, whole. It holds three things: the commit before it, called its parent, the index it produced, and when it was made. What it changed is the difference between its index and its parent's. Following parents back walks the whole history of the field, one change at a time.

```json
{ "kind": "commit", "parent": "sha256-b1…", "at": "2026-11-01T10:12:00Z",
  "index": "sha256-e8…" }
```

A commit does not say who made it. A change is made by a program's run, and the run records the commits it made, so the run is what connects a commit to the program behind it. The run is kept in the home of whoever ran it, which is often not the store the commit lands in, so the link runs from the run to the commit, never back.

A type is a schema in the field: the structure a holon's data has. Data is by its nature structure, and types are what let a field hold structure of its own making, declared in the field itself, so a type is a holon too. Programs need data, and types are what they find it by.

*The author's, 2026-11-01: type is what allows you to create schemas within the field, what allows for structure, and that is what programs need. How a type is written, and how the store checks a holon against it, is [open](ref:01M6F8G0M0D9XYVG6X8PKDAYE2).*

Each field a type declares is said in prose as well as in structure: what the key means, beside the shape the engine checks. A field is where holons connect, so the fields are the field's ontological connectors, and holons joined at them form a larger ontology, readable by a person, a program or a language model alike.

*The author's, 2026-11-02: the fields of a holon are contact points for prose, so that we can build ontologically upon them; where each holon connects are the ontological connectors, forming larger ontology. That the prose stands beside the checked shape, and models read it, the session's proposal of the same day, which he answered yes.*

A type's fields are to stand beside its identity, out of its body, as its mould, since they say what other holons hold and not what the type itself holds; a cast, but for what comes from it. A holon is then a type by having a mould, and the type of types is let go.

*The author's, 2026-11-05: fields goes out of the body; being a type both by being an instance of Type and by having fields was double, so yes, we drop the type type; mould for now. Not yet built, as [the store](ref:01M6F8G0M0CX3N7XTB02CKMPWR) tells.*
body.title: Type

body.prose:
A brief's paragraphs, a list in it, an image, a word that stands for something: each is a holon of its own, held by the brief, typed, and drawn by the component its type finds. Inside them is only what is not a holon: values, shaped by the holon's mould, text and the references among it, an image's caption, code's language. So the field holds holons and values within them, and nothing between.

*The author's, 2026-11-05: good, that leaves us with indexing; his critiques of the interior the session first proposed decided it, and the count of holons it costs is still to be measured.*
body.title: What is finer than a holon

body.prose:
Glass rests on what matters most to it, and what decides that is its ontology: what exists in it, held as knowledge in language that a knowledge graph can be built on. That is the primitives. Everything else keeps, runs or draws them, and each part should be as separate as the primitives it serves, and read as what it is.

*The author's, [2026-11-02](ref:01M6F8G0M0PTTHC2G0M03025AQ), given as a little philosophy for the culture glass grows in; the wording the session's.*

body.prose:
Does the store have to be written for the engine to have its own store?

If not we may consider other than TypeScript, for speed, anyway, or the future language stack of glass may grow from.

I'm 100% open to augmenting the markdown if need be until prose becomes its own small primitives.

The wiki can be born in when the human has a reasonable way to actually navigate it. The effort of that is to be weighed against if there are any big blocker in going so far ahead and executing, but naturally doing it in a TDD way, well orchestrated agentic way etc...
body.title: Toward building

body.prose:
Where the reader looks is the page's address, so going back and forward is only the address changing, and a reload lands where the address says. What the reader has looked at is kept in the home as their history, a holon each move adds a visit to and nothing rewrites; the root mount holds only what is the reader's, the component it calls and what it offers, and no longer changes with every move.

*Reasoned, the session's, 2026-11-01, answering the author's question of what a virtual history stack means; the root's versions were the history from 2026-11-03 until the author found, the same night, that walking back by writing old versions again is not real history, since commits are a line you can't reverse, [said](ref:01M6HP9PNA0FGNZ6W8DEJ51TX5). As [the interface](ref:01M6JZY20ZJAAP3CBJ4KRDBXFD) tells.*
